function: Target AoA/AoD estimation for bistatic sensing, not one of the seven areas. p. 2: "a new DL technique for sensing parameter estimation, i.e. the AoAs and AoDs"
notes: Excluded for function, the first code that applies. source_type, survey, no_learning and above_phy do not apply: a learned physical-layer estimator is proposed and evaluated (p. 2: "The DL model employs complex-valued neural networks"). The learned method estimates the AoA and AoD of radar targets at a bistatic radar unit that reuses the BS downlink OFDM signal. p. 1: "we focus on estimating both angle of arrival (AoA) and angle of departure (AoD)". p. 4: "an existing infrastructure is performing communication tasks, whereas a radar unit is installed to estimate the sensing parameters of the different targets". This is direction estimation for sensing, close to the excluded "direction-of-arrival estimation alone". It is not area 5 because the learned method designs no beam, waveform or resource, and the transmitted signal is an ordinary communication signal. p. 3: "the radar receiver utilizes the backscattered communication signal for precise estimation of target sensing parameters". It is not area 2 because the channel is estimated with classical LS and only the sensing block is learned. p. 4: "the channel estimation is performed according to the well-known least squares". p. 5: "the channel estimation and the coarse timing estimation, are indeed classical approaches". The metrics are angle MSE (rad^2) against the CRB and the accuracy of classifying the number of targets per peak (pp. 10-11). No communication metric is reported. For the reviewer: the system does communicate (the BS serves users, p. 3), so the example "sensing alone in a system that does not communicate" does not apply literally. The exclusion rests on the learned function, which is none of the seven. Identity: the PDF is arXiv:2404.00582v1 by Naoumi, Bazzi, Bomfin and Chafii, and its header (p. 1) states acceptance in IEEE JSTSP in March 2024, which is consistent with the DOI. The DOI itself is not printed in the PDF.
